samples.summary: Import dry-run previews still interpolate the `--replace` doc id unencoded, so they no longer match the request `HttpClient` now sends
samples.evidence: The diff establishes the invariant "every identifier interpolated into a preview path goes through `seg()`" (packages/cli/src/client/dry-run.ts) and the client now encodes ids (`putDocContent` → `/documents/${seg(docId)}/content`, http-client.ts:303). Three out-of-diff preview sites were not updated and still print the raw id: packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:155 `path: `/documents/${replace}/content``, packages/cli/src/notes/import.ts:147, packages/cli/src/slides/import.ts:182. For a `--replace` id containing `/`, `?` or `..`, `docs|notes|slides import --replace <id> --dry-run` prints a path different from the one the real run fetches — exactly the divergence the change says it removes, and which docs/design/cli.md:836-841 now claims cannot happen.

samples.summary: `apiKeysUrl()` re-implements the api-key management URL that `HttpClient` builds, so the two can silently drift
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts:13-18 builds `${server}/workspaces/${config.workspace}/api-keys[/${seg(keyId)}]` by hand, duplicating the three independent constructions in packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:397 (listApiKeys), :404 (createApiKey) and :415 (revokeApiKey). Nothing ties them together: if the management route ever moves (e.g. under `/api/v1`), the preview keeps printing the old URL while the real request goes elsewhere, defeating the stated 'the preview is the request' invariant. A single exported URL builder on `HttpClient` consumed by both would remove the drift; the fix belongs on the new code.

samples.summary: New dry-run early returns placed outside the command's own try/catch, unlike every other command in the package
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:20-32, packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:125-128 and packages/cli/src/commands/tabs.ts:14-17 call `getConfig(opts)` (which reads/parses the on-disk profile via resolveConfig, packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:77) before entering `try { ... } catch (e) { outputError(e) }`. Every other dry-run branch in the package sits inside the try. A throw here bypasses the command's own error envelope and falls through to the last-resort catch in packages/cli/src/cli.ts:90 — same envelope in the real binary, but any caller that drives `program.parseAsync` directly (e.g. the helper in packages/cli/test/read-dry-run.test.ts:44) gets a rejected promise instead of an enveloped error.

samples.summary: `seg()` now exists twice — exported from dry-run.ts and duplicated privately in http-client.ts
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/client/dry-run.ts:11 exports `seg`, and packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:30 declares an identical private copy. The whole point of the change is that preview and request encode identically; two independent definitions is the mechanism by which they can stop doing so. http-client.ts:268 (`downloadFileDocument`) also still calls `encodeURIComponent` inline rather than `seg`, a third spelling of the same rule.

finding.summary: Design doc now asserts a blanket "a dry run never reaches the network" contract, but six sibling read commands outside the diff still fetch under --dry-run
finding.evidence: The change is accompanied by docs/design/cli.md:824-827 ("Reads honour the flag too … A dry run never reaches the network, so it burns no rate limit and emits no access log even when the command is harmless"), and the new test header repeats it. That universal claim is false for the read commands the diff did not touch, all of which call the client with no `opts.dryRun` guard: packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:40 (`slides list`), slides.ts:81 (`slides get`), packages/cli/src/commands/notes.ts:35 (`notes list`), notes.ts:76 (`notes get`), packages/cli/src/commands/files.ts:85 (`files list`), files.ts:105 (`files get`), and packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:39 (`sheets export`, which issues GET /cells before writing the file). An agent that reads the new doc sentence and pre-flights `slides list --dry-run` or `sheets export … --dry-run` still hits the API — and `sheets export` additionally writes the output file. Fix belongs either on those call sites or on the new doc wording (narrow it to the four commands actually changed).

verdict.reason:
The finding's core factual claim — that the six/seven sibling read commands "call the client with no `opts.dryRun` guard" — is false in the current tree. Every cited site has an `if (opts.dryRun) { printDryRun(...); return; }` early return placed *before* the `getClient(opts).<method>()` call:

- `slides list`: guard at packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:40-45, client call at :46 (the reviewer cited :40 as the unguarded fetch — it is the guard itself).
- `slides get`: guard at slides.ts:87-90, client call at :91.
- `notes list`: guard at packages/cli/src/commands/notes.ts:35-40, client call at :41.
- `notes get`: guard at notes.ts:82-85, client call at :86.
- `files list`: guard at packages/cli/src/commands/files.ts:87-92, client call at :93.
- `files get`: guard at files.ts:113-116, client call at :117.
- `sheets export`: guard at packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:44-56 (mirrors `getCells` URL incl. range encoding), client call at :58 and `writeFileSync` at :70 — both unreachable under `--dry-run`, so the claimed "additionally writes the output file" is also false.

A repo-wide grep over packages/cli/src/commands confirms the same pattern for every other read command named in the doc sentence: `files download` (files.ts:58 before the runner at :62), `notes content` (:145 before :150), `notes export` (:205 before :209), `docs list/get/content/export` (docs.ts:78/125/194/256 each before :85/:130/:203/:265), `sheets tabs list` (tabs.ts:14 before :19), `sheets cells get` (cells.ts:20 before :36-39), and `api-keys list` (api-keys.ts:52 before :56). The doc statement at docs/design/cli.md:824-830 therefore matches the implementation; there is no unupdated caller or bypassing entry point.
